text:
Mia: Heads up — noticed a ~12% delta in shadowed cohort invoices for yesterday's pricing experiment. digging in now, but flagging because it might affect the rollout numbers.
Omar: Hmm 12% is big. any idea if it's billing-side (metering) or ingestion (shadow traffic tagging)?
Mia: Initial look shows most of the delta comes from two customers in cohort B — large embedding jobs. their usage looks fine in prod logs but the shadow meter shows extra token counts.
Sophia: @Mia can you paste the sample request ids? i want to compare gateway logs vs billing events.
Mia: sample ids: r-034ef, r-034f0, r-034f7.
Mia: snippet from gateway: ```GET /v1/embeddings 200 token_count=124502 req_id=r-034ef```
Mia: corresponding billing event: ```billing.event: embeddings.create token_count=248,976 req_ref=r-034ef shadow=true```
Raj: doubling of token_count on billing event. looks like a join/aggregation issue in the shadow pipeline. cc @Omar to check ETL.
Omar: I'll check the shadow-ingest Lambda and the batch aggregator. quick hypothesis: we split long documents into chunks in gateway and aggregator double-counts chunk boundaries for shadow pipeline.
Sophia: If that's true, it would only affect shadow cohorts and not production charges, right?
Mia: Correct. but our rollout analytics and experiment metrics use shadow billing to project revenue impact, so experiment decision could be skewed.
Raj: For immediate ops: can we rollback experiment gating and pause traffic to cohort B until we confirm?
Omar: We can pause splitting on shadow path by flipping flag SHADOW_CHUNK_NORMALIZE=false — but need a deploy window. alternatively rate-limit cohort B to 10% until we patch aggregator.
Mia: Let's do the rate-limit short-term. I don't want full rollback until we confirm scope.
Sophia: Agreed. Mia can you open a minimal support ticket to affected accounts informing them of a possible billing projection discrepancy? templated message ok.
Mia: Drafting now. will tag for legal review.
Raj: Omar — priority: verify aggregator logic and produce a diff of token sums between gateway and billing for last 72h. include per-request breakdown.
Omar: On it. ETA 45m.
billing-bot: Incident created: FIN-2241 — "shadow billing token double-count" assigned to Omar, priority P2. link: https://redwood.example/incidents/FIN-2241
Mia: Also: we should check grandfathering rules. if we change pricing mid-rollout we might misclassify legacy credits when reconciling.
Sophia: Good call. @Mia please add the grandfathering flag status for cohorts in the ticket.
Mia: Added — cohort B: grandfather=false; cohort A (control): grandfather=true for legacy credits.
Raj: For postmortem: include impact on experiment decision, vendor/ETL check, and a reconciliation playbook (steps to adjust projections once corrected).
Omar: Found the bug: aggregator uses a naive sum join on chunk ids and fails to dedupe when chunk metadata is missing — pushing a patch to dedupe by (req_ref, chunk_index). will deploy to staging.
Sophia: Great. after patch, run backfill on the 48h shadow events and report corrected delta.
Mia: If backfill reduces delta to <2% then we proceed with planned canary tomorrow. if >5% we delay and re-evaluate.
Raj: Approvals: finance ok with rate-limit. product signoff pending a quick note from PM.
Mia: PM (Ethan) pinged and approved conservative rate-limit.
Omar: Patch deployed to staging, running validation scripts now. validation command: ```scripts/validate_shadow_counts --since 2024-03-20 --ids r-034ef,r-034f0,r-034f7```
Mia: Thanks everyone. will update FIN-2241 with the backfill results. :thumbsup:
Sophia: Thanks — looping in customer success if we need outreach for any affected invoices.
billing-bot: Backfill job queued: job-8872, estimate 27m.
